content.title: About
content.content: Chocolate pudding is a ready‑to‑eat dessert made from milk, sugar and cocoa mass. It has a smooth, creamy texture and a rich chocolate flavor, usually served chilled. The product is shelf‑stable until opened and only needs refrigeration after opening.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first ready‑to‑eat puddings appeared in the United States in the early 20th century as a quick dessert for busy families.
Chocolate pudding is often used in cooking shows as a base for decorative and layered desserts.
Ready‑made pudding typically contains 10–15 % cocoa, making it milder than pure dark chocolate.
In many countries it is served with whipped cream or fresh berries for a flavor contrast.
Aluminum foil packaging helps preserve aroma and freshness for up to 12 months.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: The milk base provides calcium, essential for bone and tooth health.

items.title: Contains magnesium
items.content: Magnesium supports normal muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Quick energy
items.content: Pudding supplies carbohydrates and a modest amount of fat for rapid energy replenishment.

items.title: Antioxidants from cocoa
items.content: Cocoa contains flavonoids that may help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Mood‑enhancing
items.content: Chocolate stimulates serotonin production, which can improve mood.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: High sugar levels can contribute to weight gain and increase the risk of dental caries.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: The dairy base may cause discomfort for people who are lactose intolerant.

items.title: Cocoa allergy
items.content: A small number of individuals may experience allergic reactions to cocoa.

items.title: Preservatives
items.content: Some ready‑made puddings contain additives that may be undesirable for sensitive individuals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The pudding is ready to eat straight from the package. It can be enjoyed on its own, added to fruit salads, used as a layer in cakes, or topped with whipped cream and berries.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the pudding in the refrigerator at 2–4 °C. After opening, consume within 3–5 days. Do not freeze, as the texture may change.
